q: Some pearlfish find shelter by entering which living animal through its anus?
d: The fish uses the cucumber’s hollow, water-filled body as a refuge.
evidence: Museum account describes pearlfish sheltering in sea-cucumber anal openings.

q: A threatened sea apple can swell dramatically. What escape route can this enable?
d: Swelling makes the animal easier for moving water to pick up.
evidence: Museum account explicitly links swelling with transport by currents.

q: Snake sea cucumbers lack ordinary tube feet. What helps them cling to surfaces?
d: Their flexible bodies carry microscopic anchoring structures.
evidence: Synaptids attach with small skin hooks called sclerites.

q: A remarkable oyster specimen at London’s Natural History Museum contains a pearl formed around what entire animal?
d: The oyster coated an intruding pearlfish in mother-of-pearl, preserving its outline.
s: Natural History Museum · The fish that is also a pearl
evidence: Curator describes a pearlfish entombed by nacre inside an oyster.

q: A flower urchin delivers venom mainly through which structures?
d: Its flowerlike pedicellariae conceal short spines and deliver the venom.
evidence: Museum curator distinguishes venomous pedicellariae from ordinary spine delivery.

q: What living item has the carrier crab Dorippe frascone been seen wearing as protection?
d: The crab carries the spiny animal above its body.
evidence: Museum account explicitly records sea urchins carried like protective hats.

q: What unusual maintenance feature do a sea urchin’s grazing teeth possess?
d: Its complex chewing apparatus keeps scraping surfaces effective as the teeth wear.
choices: They are replaced after every meal
They are sharpened against neighboring teeth
They are polished by swallowed sand
evidence: Museum describes five self-sharpening teeth in Aristotle’s lantern.

q: Why do pearl octopuses nest near the warm seeps at California’s deep-sea Octopus Garden?
d: Warmer water shortens incubation, reducing the time embryos remain vulnerable.
choices: More oxygen dissolves in the warmer water
Minerals from the springs harden egg coverings
The springs repel all egg parasites
evidence: Monitoring found faster egg development at warm thermal springs.

q: How can a hagfish wipe excess slime from its own slippery body?
d: The flexible fish ties its body into a knot and moves it along its length.
choices: Inflate and shed its outer skin
Scrape itself with a tail spine
evidence: Institutional account explicitly describes knot sliding to remove slime.

q: Greater sac-winged bat mothers adjust their calls when addressing pups in a behavior compared with what human habit?
d: Pup-directed calls differ in pitch and sound quality from calls to adults.
s: Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute · Bat babble
evidence: Researchers report distinct maternal vocalizations directed toward babbling pups.

q: Some Shark Bay dolphins protect their snouts while searching the seafloor with what removable tool?
d: The sponge acts as a protective cover while the dolphin probes for fish.
s: NOAA Ocean Today · Dolphins use tools
evidence: Transcript describes basket sponges worn over beaks to prevent scrapes and stings.

q: Shark Bay dolphins sometimes lift a large empty sea-snail shell and shake it to obtain what?
d: The shell becomes a container from which the dolphin tips out a meal.
s: NOAA Ocean Today · Dolphins use tools
evidence: NOAA transcript reports conch shells trapping fish then shaken into dolphin mouths.

q: In a classic visual-learning experiment, pigeons distinguished new paintings by which pair of artists after training?
d: Their discrimination extended to paintings they had not encountered during training.
s: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior · Watanabe et al., 1995
evidence: Primary abstract read; novel Monet/Picasso paintings discriminated after training.

q: In a 2016 study, archerfish learned to distinguish which unfamiliar kind of image from dozens of alternatives?
d: They learned the rewarded face even when obvious features such as overall head shape and color were standardized.
s: University of Queensland · Archerfish face discrimination
evidence: University study account describes learned faces among novel distractors; controlled color and head shape.

q: In a Berlin laboratory study, rats learned both roles in which familiar children’s game?
d: They searched for a person or chose hiding places themselves, with playful interaction as a reward.
s: Einstein Center for Neurosciences Berlin · Rats play hide and seek
evidence: First-party report describes rats learning seeker and hider roles.

q: During mixed-species hunts, day octopuses have been filmed displacing fish partners with what surprisingly familiar action?
d: An arm makes a rapid strike that pushes the fish away; motives can differ between encounters.
evidence: Primary indexed account reports active displacement with arm strikes during cooperative hunting.

q: How does a disco clam produce its flashing display?
d: It rolls and unrolls reflective mantle tissue, redirecting available light.
choices: Switching a chemical light reaction on and off
evidence: Museum explains reflected light from contrasting mantle sides, not bioluminescence.

q: Some freshwater mussels display a fishlike lure. What are they trying to deliver to a fish that approaches?
d: The young attach to fish gills and later leave to settle on the riverbed.
evidence: Museum describes mantle lure, larval release into fish gills and later settlement.

q: A scallop’s eyes focus light using which arrangement familiar from some telescopes?
d: Ordered layers of guanine crystals form the reflecting surfaces inside its many eyes.
evidence: Primary abstract details concave image-forming mirrors tiled by square guanine crystals.

q: Zola, an animal trained at St Andrews, copied notes from Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star. What was she?
d: Researchers trained seals to modify their vocal sounds to match melodies and human vowel sounds.
s: University of St Andrews · Grey seals copy human speech and music
evidence: University report names Zola and documents melody copying.

q: In a breakfast-planning experiment, scrub-jays cached more evening food in which place?
a: Where breakfast had previously been unavailable
d: The birds provisioned the location associated with a foodless morning, consistent with anticipating a later need.
choices: Where breakfast had previously been unavailable
Only where they were currently eating
Whichever compartment was nearest the door
evidence: Primary paper reports significantly more cached pine nuts in no-breakfast compartment.

q: When mobbed by damselfish, a mimic octopus has been observed exposing two banded arms in an imitation of what?
d: The rest of its body remains concealed while the arms resemble the threatening animal.
s: Proceedings of the Royal Society B · Norman et al., 2001
evidence: Primary indexed paper describes banded sea-snake posture during damselfish attacks.

q: Small blanket octopuses have been seen carrying weapons stolen from which animal?
d: They carry pieces of its stinging tentacles while remaining unaffected by the venom.
s: University of Texas Marine Science Institute · Big Blanket
evidence: University account describes tentacle theft by males and young females.

q: What does a male blanket octopus leave with a female to fertilize her eggs later?
d: The female can retain the specialized arm until she is ready to use its sperm.
choices: A sealed shell full of sperm
s: University of Texas Marine Science Institute · Big Blanket
evidence: University account describes arm detachment and storage by females.

q: Female argonaut octopuses deliberately collect what at the sea surface to control buoyancy?
d: They trap a bubble, then dive until pressure compresses it enough to balance their weight.
s: Proceedings of the Royal Society B · Finn and Norman, 2010
evidence: Primary indexed abstract describes surface air capture, sealing and depth-dependent buoyancy.
